source_document: data/ISO_IEC_30173_2023(en) Digital twin - Concepts and terminology.pdf (ISO/IEC 30173:2023(en), Digital twin - Concepts and terminology)
role_in_kg: digital_twin_vocabulary_root: the concepts-and-terminology basis for the Cognitive Digital Twin target of the whole use case. Supplies the digital twin / target entity / synchronization / control loop / analytics vocabulary; the asset digital twin type corresponds to the ISO 19650 AIM, DT synchronization corresponds to ISO 19650-3 AIM-asset alignment, and the Clause 7 functional loop is the PdM spine stated in DT terms.

extraction_notes.registry_scope: Reconciliation registry is the union of the eleven preceding extraction files. Reused rather than re-noded: asset (3.1.18 wording aligns with the ISO 55000/19650 asset definitions - the SUBTYPE_OF entity edge is the unifying assertion), data (3.2.1 ISO/IEC 2382 wording differs from ISO 55000 3.1.10 'facts about an object' - same concept, noted), asset data (3.2.2 vs ISO 55013 3.1 - same concept), information model (3.3.3 ISO 6707-2 source vs ISO 19650-1 - same concept family), life cycle (3.1.11 vs ISO 19650-1/ISO 55000), interoperability (3.4.3 vs ISO 55013 3.6), monitoring (3.5.5 refines ISO 55000 3.3.25 with supervision-and-alarming of the target entity - captured as edges, not a fork), object (3.1.19 vs ISO 55000 3.1.9). The ISO 19650-5 cyber-physical system node is upgraded IN PLACE with the proper 30173 3.5.10 term definition and definition_provenance (SAMP/AMP precedent).
extraction_notes.id_convention: Keeps term_<snake_case> and the Function label for the stakeholder node. Semiotics terms carry the '(semiotics)' qualifier (concept/symbol/phenomenon are ultra-generic names). No new labels, no new relationship types.
extraction_notes.verbatim_convention: All definitions are verbatim ISO/IEC 30173:2023 text (inline cross-reference numbers elided; non-contiguous quotes joined by ' [...] '), asserted at build time and enforced by backend/gates/verify_verbatim.py. The source's own typo 'entitiy' (3.1.5) is quoted as printed. Figures 1-4 are captured as edges (system context, life cycle, stakeholders, functional view), not nodeified.
extraction_notes.structure_notes: Terms deliberately not noded: 5.2 advantages list (note-level), Annex A definition comparison and Annex B semiotics exposition (informative), the nine individual stakeholder roles (summarized on the single Function node), and the 5.6 life cycle stage names (enumeration values, kept in the life-cycle-process node's verbatim definition).
extraction_notes.bsdd_mapping: Checked against the buildingSMART Data Dictionary via api.bsdd.buildingsmart.org TextSearch (2026-08-05): no genuine matches - bSDD has no digital-twin vocabulary entry. Absence means checked-no-genuine-match, per backend/gates/verify_bsdd.py.
extraction_notes.merge_note: File name does not match the iso19650-* union glob; it is listed explicitly in the union tooling and must always be loaded together with the other eleven files.

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: digital twin
nodes.definition: digital representation of a target entity with data connections that enable convergence between the physical and digital states at an appropriate rate of synchronization
nodes.note: Note 1 to entry: digital twin has some or all of the capabilities of connection, integration, analysis, simulation, visualization, optimization, collaboration, etc. Note 2: can provide an integrated view throughout the life cycle of the target entity. 5.3.5 (verbatim): 'a digital twin can combine the data collection of the IoT, the processing of big data and the modelling and analysis of AI to evaluate the current state, diagnose the problems in the past, give the analysis results, simulate various possibilities, and predict the future trend.' - the sentence the Cognitive Digital Twin use case operationalizes.

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: entity
nodes.definition: thing (physical or non-physical) having a distinct existence
nodes.note: Domain qualifier <digital twin>. EXAMPLE: person, object, event, idea, process, etc. [SOURCE: ISO/IEC 20924:2021, 3.1.18, modified.]

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: target entity
nodes.definition: entity providing a functional purpose in reality which is the subject of digital representation
nodes.note: Note 1 to entry: the target entity, which provides some functional purpose in reality, can be either physical or digital under consideration. In the PdM use case the target entity is the maintainable asset streamed by the condition monitoring system.

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: physical entity
nodes.definition: entity in the physical world that can be the subject of sensing and/or actuating

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: digital entity
nodes.definition: computational entitiy comprising data elements and procedural elements
nodes.note: The source's own typo 'entitiy' is quoted as printed.

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: physical domain
nodes.definition: classification of physical entities under consideration

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: digital domain
nodes.definition: classification of digital entities under consideration
nodes.note: Note 1 to entry: entities in the digital domain can be embedded in a physical domain.

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: digital representation
nodes.definition: digital entity representing either a set of properties or behaviours or both of one or more observable elements

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: modelling
nodes.definition: using symbolic paradigms or formal languages to create an abstract representation of a thing

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: ecosystem
nodes.definition: infrastructure and services based on a network of organizations and stakeholders
nodes.note: Note 1 to entry: organizations can include public bodies. [SOURCE: ISO/IEC TS 27570:2021, 3.8].

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: semantics
nodes.definition: rules that provide the intended meaning of entities or things to construct, deploy and use

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: semiotics
nodes.definition: study of signs and their properties including the relationships between the domains of symbols, concepts and cyber-physical phenomena

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: control loop
nodes.definition: feedback link between digital entities and target entities whereby the digital entity receives data from the target entity and issues back to the target entity data that are used to modify the behaviour of the target entity
nodes.note: Domain qualifier <digital twin>. Note 1 to entry: control loops use engineering control methods for the purpose of automation, e.g. to keep the temperature on an engine under control of a certain limit.

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: concept (semiotics)
nodes.definition: semantic artifact that represents meaning of a symbol, a thing or a phenomenon

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: symbol (semiotics)
nodes.definition: ontological artifact that denotes a certain meaning, a thing or a phenomenon

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: phenomenon (semiotics)
nodes.definition: thing artifact that is symbolized by an ontological symbol and has implemented certain concepts

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: synchronization
nodes.definition: action of making the states of target entity and digital entity synchronized, using network for real time system
nodes.note: Domain qualifier <digital twin>.

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: digital twin system
nodes.definition: system providing functionalities for the digital twin composed of inter-operating target entities, digital entities, data connections, and models, data and interfaces involved in the data connection process
nodes.note: 5.5.2: contains at least one target entity and its digital entity, with their synchronization and interaction with stakeholders to improve one or some performance indicators of the target entities in one or some life cycle stages. 5.5.5 infrastructure: sensors, actuators, networks, geographic information systems. 5.5.6 system aspects: integration, governance, security and privacy, and data ethics.

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: big data
nodes.definition: data set(s) with characteristics (e.g. volume, velocity, variety, variability, veracity, etc.) that for a particular problem domain at a given point in time cannot be efficiently processed using traditional technologies and techniques in order to extract value
nodes.note: [SOURCE: ISO/IEC 38505-1:2017, 3.2, modified.]

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: statistics model
nodes.definition: model that uses mathematical analysis tools to build a representation of the data for the purpose of conducting analysis to infer any relationships between variables or discover insights

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: engineering model
nodes.definition: model that includes geometry, materials, components and behaviour relevant throughout the entity life cycle

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: verification
nodes.definition: confirmation, through the provision of objective evidence, that specified requirements have been fulfilled
nodes.note: [SOURCE: ISO 9000:2015, 3.8.12, modified.]

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: validation
nodes.definition: confirmation, through the provision of objective evidence, that the requirements for a specific intended use or application have been fulfilled
nodes.note: [SOURCE: ISO 9000:2015, 3.8.13, modified.]

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: visualization
nodes.definition: use of computer graphics and image processing to present models or characteristics of processes or objects
nodes.note: Note 1 to entry: visualization tools are provided to support human understanding. [SOURCE: ISO 23247-4:2021, 3.4, modified.]

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: optimization
nodes.definition: design and operation of a system or process to improve its efficiency or effectiveness

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: prediction
nodes.definition: process of computation used to obtain the predicted value(s) of a quantity
nodes.note: Note 1 to entry: the term 'prediction' can also be used to denote the predicted value(s) of a quantity. [SOURCE: IEC 62059-31-1:2008, 3.27].

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: simulation
nodes.definition: use of a similar or equivalent system to imitate a real system, so that it behaves like or appears to be the real system
nodes.note: Note 1 to entry: simulation serves the purpose of analysing the future behaviour of a system, i.e. making predictions, or the purpose of reasoning on the past behaviour in order to analyse failures. 5.3.3 (verbatim): 'simulation is one of the core technologies for creating and running a digital twin with predictive capabilities.'

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: augmented reality
nodes.definition: virtual objects superimposed upon or composited with the real world
nodes.note: Note 1 to entry: virtual and real-world objects co-exist in augmented reality systems. [SOURCE: ISO/IEC TR 23843:2020, 3.3].

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: virtual reality
nodes.definition: artificial environment presented in the computer
nodes.note: [SOURCE: ISO/IEC TR 18121:2015, 3.6].

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: analytics
nodes.definition: predicting, reasoning, and controlling the behaviour (current and future) of an asset or process via both physics and artificial intelligence or machine learning models
nodes.note: The vocabulary-level description of what the predictive-maintenance analytical model does.

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: Internet of Things
nodes.definition: infrastructure of interconnected entities, people, systems and information resources together with services which processes and reacts to information from the physical world and digital world
nodes.note: [SOURCE: ISO/IEC 20924:2021, 3.2.4, modified.] 5.3.5 (verbatim): 'IoT is the underlying associated technology of digital twin, and it is the necessary condition for the digital twin interaction with target entities.'

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: infrastructure
nodes.definition: system of facilities, equipment and services needed for the operation of an entity
nodes.note: [SOURCE: ISO 9000:2015, 3.5.2, modified.]

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: semiotic triangle
nodes.definition: The semiotic triangle is a visualization of the relationships between the phenomenon of interest and the intended semantic concept, that is, the conceptual meaning of that phenomenon, and the intended semantics of the phenomenon of interest.
nodes.note: 5.3.1.1: the explicit expression of concept, phenomenon and symbol are necessary to define structure and behaviour of a target entity by using tools such as semantics + engineering + ontologies; if these tools are not utilized, the life cycle of the target entity has unavoidable gaps. Annex B expands on semiotics.

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: digital twin life cycle process
nodes.definition: The life cycle of a digital entity shall include inception, design and development, verification and validation, deployment, operation and monitoring, re-evaluation and retirement.
nodes.note: The life cycle of a target entity shall include development, verification and validation, deployment, operation and monitoring, re-evaluation and recycling; the two life cycles are distinct and do not align at all milestones. Changes in the digital entity can be iteratively fed back to design and development; the flow between digital and target entity does not have to be fully automatic and can include a human-in-the-loop sometimes (5.6).

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: component digital twin
nodes.definition: The component digital twin is typically a major element that has a significant impact on the performance of the target entity to which it belongs.
nodes.note: EXAMPLE: a component digital twin can relate to a complex motor or pump within a system, where the system itself has a separate system-level digital twin.

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: asset digital twin
nodes.definition: Asset digital twin can be collections of component digital twins and can consist of component digital twins. Asset digital twins provide visibility at the unit level.
nodes.note: NOTE (5.7.3): where an asset consists of a single component, it can be considered both an asset digital twin and a component digital twin. The Cognitive Digital Twin readiness audit in this repo checks whether an IFC model can seed exactly this: an asset digital twin over the maintainable plant.

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: system digital twin
nodes.definition: A system digital twin is a collection of target entities and digital entities that together perform a system- or network-wide function. A system digital twin provides visibility into a set of interconnected or interdependent target entities.

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: process digital twin
nodes.definition: A process digital twin is a digital twin that provides a view into a set of activities or operations.
nodes.note: Can consist of a set of physical entities or system digital twins, but focuses more on the process itself rather than the physical entities.

nodes.label: Function
nodes.name: digital twin stakeholder
nodes.definition: stakeholders that play distinct organizational roles in the digital twin value chain, including digital twin system stakeholders (6.2) and ecosystem partners (6.3)
nodes.note: 6.2 system stakeholders: developers (requirements analysis, planning and design, development, testing and verification), resource providers, integrators, users, operators (problem discovery, fault resolution, maintenance, and the establishment of a fault knowledge base). 6.3 ecosystem partners: infrastructure provider, service provider, standards development organization, government and community.

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.name: digital twin functional loop
nodes.definition: Digital twin systems can be created by digitalizing and simulating target entities in the digital domain, establishing connections between the target entities and digital entities, and forming a closed or open loop by gathering data from the physical domain, integrating optimization in the digital domain, then making decisions, and applying adjustments to the physical domain based on those decisions.
nodes.note: The functional view of the digital twin - and, term for term, the PdM spine: gather condition data from the physical domain, analyse in the digital domain, decide, and apply maintenance adjustments back to the asset.

cross_references.series: Companion document: ISO/IEC TR 30172 (Digital twin - Use cases). The functional view (Clause 7) is elaborated by the Digital Twin reference architecture standard. AAS (asset administration shell) is named as an interoperable manifestation of a digital twin in manufacturing (5.4.2.1).
cross_references.pdm_anchor: The CDT chain is now closed in vocabulary: IFC model -> ISO 19650 AIM -> (CORRESPONDS_TO) asset digital twin; condition telemetry -> synchronization (CORRESPONDS_TO AIM-asset alignment); PdM analytical model -> analytics (3.5.8, physics + AI/ML); RUL prediction -> prediction (3.5.3); alert/work-order feedback -> control loop (3.1.14); the whole spine -> the Clause 7 functional loop.
